title: Functions, scope, closures and the value of `this`

videos.script:
This is the lesson the rest of the language leans on. {{values}} In JavaScript a function is a value, like a number or a string. You can store it in a variable, pass it to another function, and return it from one.

That last part has a consequence nobody expects at first. {{closure}} A function returned from another function still remembers the variables it could see where it was written, even after the function that made them has finished. That memory is called a closure. Event handlers use it. Timers use it. Every framework you will learn after this course is built on it.

Then there is this. {{this}} Inside a function, the word this means something that depends not on where the function was written, but on how it was called. Call the same function two ways and you get two different answers. {{arrow}} Arrow functions are the exception, and that exception is why they exist.

By the end you will be able to read an error like cannot read properties of undefined, reading prefix, and know at once that a method lost its object on the way.
